checks.check: code review of TargetWalk and the oracle, existing paths unchanged, tests
checks.evidence: Read the full diff. Rows: E_t = u P1 + z G + b Q with u an integer and z, b mod r; key = abscissa+1 (PrimeCurve::key >> 1), sign bit dropped, so one key per negation orbit; collision recomputed from the coefficients, plus = (E1 == -E2) uses the sum of coefficient triples, else the difference, so du*s1 + db*logQ + dz = 0, stored as Row{columns: du*coef_of, a: -dz, b: -db} with the loop's convention du*coef*x = h*(a + b*d) (unit test asserts it under brute-force logs). Rank test is the 2x2 determinant mod r; (du, db) = (0, 0) rows are dropped; the walk stops at rank 2 or 3T. Chained jumps: K_j = K_(j-1) + K_(j-2) with (gamma, beta) added mod r, one addition each, chain restarted on identity; J_j = alpha_j P1 + K_j charged (popcount(alpha) - 1 + 1) additions; ledgers sum to build_ops. eval() silently skips a bit beyond the doubled-multiple table, but u <= 1 + 3T*w equals the bound the table is sized from (bound check in wwalk_plan_check), so no bit is dropped. The tw=0 paths: plugins.rs adds only `if tw` branches and `self.tw_table = None`; methods.rs adds two Err checks and one help string. Own checks: (a) `cargo test --release --offline --lib -- wwalk target_walk plan_refuses` with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/ctarget-f1: 15 passed, 0 failed (cached fresh test binary, 'Finished in 0.15s'), including target_walk_rows_are_affine_stop_at_rank_two_and_solve and wwalk_target_in_walk_recovers_on_the_first_trial; (b) independent Python re-implementation of the walk algebra on the real k = 20 curve (3000 walks, plain and chained): 0 bad rows, rank 2 reached and logQ solved in 3000/3000, mean steps 1.376 and 1.387 sqrt(r), extra-row runs 6.3-6.5 % (measured: 1.378-1.412, 5.5-5.8 %); (c) own op count of set-up, walk and verification on the same curve: plain 0.949 / 1.396 / 0.256, chained 0.368 / 1.373 / 0.256 sqrt(r), vs measured 0.949 / 1.412 / 0.255 and 0.368 / 1.390 / 0.255, so the Rust ledgers charge exactly what the rules imply (no under-count); (d) `ecbench plan` refuses tw=1 without g=1 (via 'grow=2 needs g=1'), tw=1 with grow=1 and cj=1 without tw; tw=1 on a two-abscissa base passes plan and fails at run time with an explicit error record ('needs a base of exactly 1 abscissa'), never silently.

errata.issue: TargetWalk emits only table_insert_attempts and lookups. Per step it also does a sign canonicalisation (inside PrimeCurve::key), an RNG draw and two mod-r additions plus an integer addition, none counted anywhere; the 'counted:walk_bookkeeping' marker on the relations phase belongs to the relation loop's target walk, not to this table (the same gap exists in WalkTable). rho-neg's partition hash is also unlisted.
